To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the future teachers show a moderate level of positive attitudes toward refugees; 2) there is no significant relationship between the attitudes and the affective reaction; 3) the future teachers have a positive attitude toward inclusive European citizenship; 4) there is a significant relationship between the inclusive European citizenship and the attitudes toward refugees.

The future teachers have a marked indifference toward refugees and the related issues, but not a high perceived threat or marked emotional reaction; the attitudes toward refugees and the inclusive European citizenship are not very positive but the latter legitimizes the reception, equal rights and new forms of coexistences of refugees in European countries; the perceived threat is the principal predictor of an inclusive European citizenship; and finally, there is a marked correlation between the attitudes toward refugees, inclusive European citizenship and perceived threat.
the attitudes toward refugees and the inclusive European citizenship are correlated, and that the perceived threat is the principal predictor of the inclusive European citizenship.
